title: Demand theories of the fertility transition: An iconoclastic view
source_note: Population Studies 41(1):5-30. The Cleland-Wilson ideational argument: fertility fell faster and more uniformly than demand theory predicts, implicating idea/legitimation diffusion.

title: Social interactions and contemporary fertility transitions
source_note: Population and Development Review 22(4):639-682. One of A.3's four registered seminals; the social-interaction account of transition timing. Shared seminal with A.20 (channels).

title: Social learning, social influence, and new models of fertility
source_note: Population and Development Review 22(Suppl):151-175. The canonical social-learning vs social-influence distinction that defines A.3's mechanism.

title: Modelling diffusion effects in fertility transition
source_note: Population Studies 47(1):147-167. Formal diffusion model; an A.3 registered seminal.

title: Lessons from the past: Policy implications of historical fertility studies
source_note: Population and Development Review 5(2):217-245. The Princeton EFP synthesis of the language/religion clustering residual that is A.3's empirical signature.

title: The Decline of Fertility in Europe
source_note: Princeton University Press (EFP capstone volume). Book: expected Crossref-index miss; carried as the privileged channel-1 synthesis whose province studies seed anchors.

title: Diffusion Processes and Fertility Transition: Selected Perspectives
source_note: National Academies Press edited volume. Book: expected article-index miss; the second channel-1 synthesis seed. Cleland's 'Potatoes and pills' overview is a chapter here.

title: The density of social networks and fertility decisions: Evidence from South Nyanza District, Kenya
source_note: Demography 38(1):43-58. Identified social-network effect on contraceptive/fertility decisions.

title: Social norms and the fertility transition
source_note: Journal of Development Economics 80(1):1-38. Matlab, Bangladesh; one of the more credibly identified social-interaction fertility papers.

Fertility and modernity
source_note: The Economic Journal 132(642):796-833. Fertility decline diffuses along ancestral/linguistic distance from the French frontier — the cultural-boundary content signature, net of development.

title: Can internal migration foster the convergence in regional fertility rates? Evidence from nineteenth century France
source_note: The Economic Journal 129(620):1618-1692. Migration-carried diffusion of fertility control across 19th-century French departments; identified spatial diffusion.

title: Culture and the historical fertility transition
source_note: Review of Economic Studies. Culture/language and the timing of the British fertility transition; identified cultural-boundary diffusion. Year may drift 2022/2023 (VoR vs online).

title: Interaction diffusion and fertility transition in Costa Rica
source_note: Social Forces 73(2):435-462. Empirical companion to the 1993 diffusion model.
